source.title_on_document: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI

supplement.where: No separate supplement is cited. Appendices A (experiment details), B (adoption-metric methods), and C (additional results, Tables 5 and 6, Figures 14-17) are on pp. 18-30 of this PDF. The pre-registration is on OSF: https://osf.io/3u8tq/overview?view_only=e1a8044dd5044bc59dd0a7d8f3fca3c2 (p. 2, footnote 1; p. 3, footnote 2).
supplement.holds: Table 5 (p. 28) holds the numeric effect sizes behind Figure 1; Table 6 (p. 30) holds the adoption-stratified effect sizes behind Figure 6. No standard errors are printed anywhere; only significance stars.

paper_design_summary: 200 Prolific participants (US or UK residents) were block-randomized in a 2 x 2 between-subjects design: write a 250-350 word short story alone (SELF) or with an in-app GPT5-mini chat assistant (AI), and receive a bonus for originality relative to other submissions (O) or for technical quality graded on a rubric (T). The paper scores the collective diversity of final submissions within each cell with a pre-registered suite of 7 embedding-based and 5 n-gram/token-based similarity metrics, computed as each participant's leave-one-out average similarity to the others in the same cell. Quality and creativity of individual stories were not scored.

studies.label: Pre-registered 2 x 2 online experiment (AI vs SELF x originality vs quality incentives), short story writing

assignment.what_was_assigned: Access to an integrated AI writing assistant during the writing phase (AI vs SELF), crossed with the bonus scheme (originality O vs technical quality T)
assignment.quote: We run a pre-registered, between-subjects experiment in which participants are assigned via block randomization to one of four conditions in a 2 x 2 factorial design
assignment.locator: p. 3, Section 3 (Experiment Design and Data); also p. 4, Section 3.2.2 ("we also randomized participants into two conditions")
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 2, footnote 1 and p. 3, footnote 2 (OSF https://osf.io/3u8tq); p. 5, Section 4: "All of the analyses in this section were pre-registered except for the results in Figure 1 (right)."; Sections 5 and 6 are labeled exploratory (pp. 8, 9)

arms.name: AI-O
arms.description: AI writing assistant (GPT5-mini chat panel beside the editor) available during the 20-minute writing phase; bonus based on originality and uniqueness relative to other submissions (top 2% $7, top 2-10% $4, top 10-25% $2).

arms.name: AI-T
arms.description: AI writing assistant available during writing; bonus based on a rubric grade for organization and technique (A $2.50, B $1.00); told they are not graded on creativity.

arms.name: SELF-O
arms.description: Plain-text editor, no AI, external AI forbidden and monitored; originality bonus.

arms.name: SELF-T
arms.description: Plain-text editor, no AI; technical-quality bonus.

participants.exclusions: Sessions ended and work was discarded for full-screen violations (5), inactivity (6 warnings), or failed attention checks in the instruction and prompt windows; a post-hoc backtracking screen excluded one SELF participant (paid but excluded). In all "we managed to filter out 29 Prolific workers" (p. 25, A.2). The paper does not state how many people were assigned before these exclusions, so 200 is recorded as analyzed and the randomized count as null. 11 submissions outside the word limit were kept (p. 20, A.1.4).
participants.who: Prolific workers aged 18+, primary language English or fluent, at least 500 prior Prolific tasks, approval rate at least 98% (p. 25, A.3); about 14-22% students by arm (Table 2).
participants.country: United States or United Kingdom residents
participants.quote: We recruited a total of n = 200 participants from Prolific, with 50 participants per group.
participants.locator: p. 3, Section 3.1; p. 5, Table 2 note ("All groups consist of n = 50 participants."); p. 25, A.2-A.3

ai_tool.name_model: OpenAI GPT5-mini (gpt5-mini, reasoning set to medium), in an in-app chat assistant
ai_tool.how_used: Side-by-side chat window next to the story editor during the writing phase only (not during brainstorming); participants had to prompt it at least once, were capped at 15 prompts, and could copy-paste within the window. 91% of AI participants asked for a full draft at least once; requests were editing 38%, drafting 30%, creative consulting 14%, mechanical 3%, other 15% (pp. 4-5, 20).

task.description: Write a 250-350 word first-person short story set within one day and centered on a decision or dilemma, after a brainstorming and outline window.
task.duration: Up to 5 minutes brainstorming (minimum 1) and up to 20 minutes writing (minimum 5), plus a 5-minute grace period to meet the word limit; about 25 minutes on average (p. 3, Section 3.1).

outcomes.name: Within-cell similarity of final submissions, all-MiniLM-L12-v2 embeddings
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Participant-level outcome Y_i = leave-one-out mean cosine similarity of participant i's final story embedding to every other story in the same cell (p. 6, Section 4.1.1). Higher = less diverse. This model is the one the paper focuses on in Section 5 and Figure 2. The same metric is also traced over time at 30-second snapshots (Figure 2b, p. 9; exploratory) and stratified by post-treatment AI adoption (Table 6, p. 30; exploratory).

contrasts.reported: Difference in mean similarity (AI-O minus SELF-O), final submissions: 0.043*** (one-sided Welch t-test, *** p < 0.01, also significant after BH). Positive = AI arm more similar, so diversity is lower with AI. Arm means only in Figure 2a (text: final-submission similarity AI-O 0.26 vs SELF-O baseline 0.22).
contrasts.locator: p. 28, Table 5 (row all-MiniLM-L12, column AI-O - SELF-O, Final); p. 7, Figure 1; pp. 8-9, Figure 2a and text

contrasts.reported: Difference in mean similarity (AI-T minus SELF-T), final submissions: 0.062*** (one-sided Welch t-test, also significant after BH). Positive = AI arm more similar (less diverse). Arm means only in Figure 2a.
contrasts.locator: p. 28, Table 5 (all-MiniLM-L12, AI-T - SELF-T, Final); p. 9, Figure 2a

contrasts.reported: Incentive contrast among AI users: AI (T - O) similarity difference 0.023** (black stars; one red star after BH adjustment). Positive = AI-T more similar, so originality pay raised diversity among AI users.
contrasts.locator: p. 28, Table 5 (all-MiniLM-L12, AI (T - O), Final); p. 8, Hypothesis 2

contrasts.reported: Incentive contrast without AI: SELF (T - O) similarity difference 0.004 (no stars).
contrasts.locator: p. 28, Table 5 (all-MiniLM-L12, SELF (T - O), Final); p. 8, Hypothesis 2

diversity_detail.metric: Leave-one-out mean pairwise cosine similarity within cell; cell-level D_g is the mean of Y_i
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each participant's final story against every other final story in the same cell (all pairs within a condition, averaged per participant)
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Two-sample one-sided Welch t-test on participant-level leave-one-out scores; significance stars only, no SE or CI printed; BH-adjusted stars also shown in Table 5. The leave-one-out scores within a cell are not independent, and the paper does not address this.
diversity_detail.notes: Sign: the paper reports similarity, so a positive difference means less diversity in the first-named group. Adoption-stratified version (Table 6, p. 30; high adoption n = 27, low n = 37, Table 4 p. 13): AI-O - SELF-O low 0.015, high 0.069***; AI-T - SELF-T low 0.051***, high 0.072***; AI-T - AI-O low 0.041**, high 0.008. Subgroups are defined on post-treatment adoption.

outcomes.name: Within-cell similarity of final submissions, other six embedding models
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Same leave-one-out cosine-similarity construction as S1-O1 with all-mpnet-base-v2, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, embeddinggemma-300m, Style-Embedding, STAR (style), and byt5 (byte-level). All pre-registered (Table 3, p. 6). The paper treats the suite as correlated views of one latent construct and does not adjust for multiple testing in the main analysis (p. 7).

contrasts.reported: AI-O - SELF-O similarity differences, Final: all-mpnet-base 0.043***, Qwen3-Embedding -0.005, embeddinggemma 0.031***, Style-Embedding -0.033, byt5 0.004**, star 0.059***. Positive = AI more similar.
contrasts.locator: p. 28, Table 5; p. 7, Figure 1; p. 28, Figure 15 (arm means)

contrasts.reported: AI-T - SELF-T similarity differences, Final: all-mpnet-base 0.076***, Qwen3-Embedding 0.027***, embeddinggemma 0.044***, Style-Embedding 0.164***, byt5 0.017***, star 0.067***.
AI (T - O) similarity differences, Final: all-mpnet-base 0.029**, Qwen3-Embedding 0.007, embeddinggemma -0.013, Style-Embedding 0.153***, byt5 -0.002, star 0.020*.
SELF (T - O) similarity differences, Final: all-mpnet-base -0.003, Qwen3-Embedding -0.025, embeddinggemma -0.026, Style-Embedding -0.044, byt5 -0.015, star 0.013*.

diversity_detail.metric: Leave-one-out mean pairwise cosine similarity within cell
diversity_detail.embedding_model: all-mpnet-base-v2; Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B; embeddinggemma-300m; Style-Embedding; STAR; byt5
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each participant's final story against every other final story in the same cell
diversity_detail.uncertainty: One-sided Welch t-test on participant-level scores; stars only; BH-adjusted stars in Table 5
diversity_detail.notes: Similarity scale: positive differences mean less diversity in the first-named group.

outcomes.name: Within-cell lexical similarity / diversity of final submissions (n-gram and token measures)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Compression ratio (gzip), self-BLEU, ROUGE-L, and n-gram diversity score (NGDS, n = 2 and n = 3), each as leave-one-out within-cell averages where pairwise (Table 3, p. 6). NGDS is the only metric where higher means more diversity. The paper says these effects "virtually disappear" at final submission and then restricts attention to embedding metrics (pp. 7-8).

contrasts.reported: AI-O - SELF-O, Final: compression ratio -0.083, self BLEU -0.001, rougel -0.003, n gram diversity score 2 0.095, n gram diversity score 3 0.103 (no stars on any).
contrasts.locator: p. 28, Table 5; p. 7, Figure 1; p. 28, Figure 15

contrasts.reported: AI-T - SELF-T, Final: compression ratio -0.100, self BLEU 0.001, rougel 0.002, n gram diversity score 2 0.083, n gram diversity score 3 0.088 (no stars).
AI (T - O), Final: compression ratio -0.016, self BLEU 0.000, rougel -0.001, NGDS2 0.004, NGDS3 0.004 (no stars).
SELF (T - O), Final: compression ratio 0.002, self BLEU -0.001, rougel -0.006, NGDS2 0.015, NGDS3 0.018 (no stars).

diversity_detail.metric: Compression ratio; self-BLEU; ROUGE-L; n-gram diversity score (sum over n of unique n-grams / all n-grams), n = 2 and 3
diversity_detail.computed_over: Leave-one-out within-cell pairwise averages for the pairwise metrics; the document does not spell out how compression ratio and NGDS are made participant-level
diversity_detail.notes: Figure 1 caption says the NGDS comparison is flipped so effect sizes are directionally consistent, but Table 5 prints NGDS as positive without stars while Figure 15 shows higher NGDS (more lexical diversity) for AI final submissions; the sign convention of the NGDS rows in Table 5 is unclear.

outcomes.name: Similarity among the AI's first full drafts versus final submissions
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Same similarity suite applied to the first valid full draft the AI produced for each AI participant who requested one, compared with final submissions. This scores AI output, not participants' submitted work. Not pre-registered (Figure 1 right, p. 5) and Section 5 is exploratory.

contrasts.reported: Table 5 "First (AI)" columns, all-MiniLM-L12: AI-O - SELF-O 0.212***, AI-T - SELF-T 0.191***, AI (T - O) -0.017. Text: AI-O first drafts average similarity 0.39 vs 0.22 in SELF-O; AI-O final 0.26; first drafts "on average being 45% more similar across all metrics" than AI-assisted final submissions.
contrasts.locator: p. 28, Table 5; p. 7, Figure 1 (right); p. 8, Hypothesis 1 paragraph; pp. 8-9, Figure 2a

diversity_detail.metric: Leave-one-out mean pairwise cosine similarity (and the other Table 3 metrics)
diversity_detail.embedding_model: all-MiniLM-L12-v2 focal; full suite in Table 5
diversity_detail.computed_over: AI first drafts within each AI cell, compared with final submissions
diversity_detail.notes: Context only: no person produced these drafts. The exact comparison behind the Table 5 "First (AI)" column is not fully specified (see open_questions).

company_involvement.description: Authors at MIT; the AI tool is OpenAI's GPT5-mini, but the document states no company funding, data, or authorship.

eligibility.reason: Participants were block-randomized to write with or without an AI assistant (crossed with an incentive factor), 200 people analyzed (50 per cell), and the pre-registered outcome is embedding- and n-gram-based similarity across participants' final stories. Only diversity is scored; no creativity or quality rating of individual stories.

one_line_finding: AI-assisted final stories were more similar to each other than stories written alone (all-MiniLM-L12 leave-one-out similarity difference 0.043 under originality pay and 0.062 under quality pay, both p < 0.01), and originality pay reduced similarity among AI users (T - O 0.023, p < 0.05) but not among unassisted writers (0.004) (p. 28, Table 5).
open_questions: How many people were assigned before the 29 Prolific workers were filtered out (p. 25)? The 200 (50 per cell) appear to be the analyzed sample only.

What exactly does the Table 5 "First (AI)" column compare? It sits under the AI - SELF headers, but Figure 1 (right) is described as first AI draft versus final submission, and the printed 0.212 (AI-O, MiniLM) matches neither 0.39 - 0.22 nor 0.39 - 0.26 from the text.
Sign convention of the NGDS rows in Table 5 (Figure 1 caption says NGDS is flipped; Figure 15 shows AI final submissions with higher NGDS).
No standard errors are printed; extraction would need posted data or arm means with SDs (Figure 2a and Figure 15 show means with error bars only).
notes: Arm-level similarity means appear only in figures (Figure 2a, p. 9; Figure 15, p. 28), apart from the MiniLM values quoted in the text on pp. 8-9. Other reported analyses not listed as outcomes because they are not creativity or diversity scored on the output: the AI adoption share A_i (fraction of final 10-grams attributable to AI, Section 6, Figure 4, Appendix B), time and prompt counts, PCA of story embeddings (Figure 2c, Figure 17), and post-survey attitudes (Section 6.3). The diversity-over-time trajectories (Figure 2b, Figure 16) are the same similarity construct on 30-second snapshots and are mentioned under S1-O1.
